items.prompt: White to move, move 8. Black has played the bishop to b7. Several quiet pawn moves are sound. Find one of three.

claims.statement: At depth 16 c3, d4 and d3 are all within 0.5 pawns of the engine's best.

hints: The bishop on b7 eyes the pawn on e4. Which moves keep e4 safe and the centre under control?
Central pawn moves are fine here.
Any of c3, d4 or d3.
items.explain: The bishop on b7 pressures e4, but e4 already has a defender in the rook on e1, so White is not forced to do anything special. Slow, flexible pawn moves keep every plan open. At depth 16 c3, d3 and d4 lie within half a pawn of each other.

items.prompt: White to move, move 12. The black queen stands on e7. Find the move the engine prefers.

claims.statement: At depth 16 the knight move to h4 is the engine's best.
After Nh4, Nxb3 and Nf5 the knight attacks the queen on e7.

hints: The knight on f3 needs two moves to reach f5. Through which square?
From h4 the knight attacks f5; from f5 it eyes the king's side.
Knight f3 to h4.
items.explain: The knight cannot reach f5 directly, so it goes to h4 first. From f5 it attacks the queen on e7 and the pawn on d6, and it sits where no black pawn attacks it yet. The engine agrees: the knight to h4 is its first choice at depth 16, with c3 a clear step behind.

items.prompt: White to move, move 16. White wants to attack on the king's side, and the queen is the piece to bring. Find the queen move.

claims.statement: At depth 16 the queen move to d2 is the engine's best.

hints: Which square for the queen leads toward g5 and also connects the pieces?
From d2 the queen reaches g5 in one more move.
Queen d1 to d2.
items.explain: From d2 the queen has the diagonal to g5 and defends the bishop on c1. The other queen move, Qe2, keeps the queen back and the engine rates it a quarter of a pawn lower. At depth 16 the move to d2 is the engine's first choice.

items.prompt: Black to move, move 23. The queen on g3 looks at the pawn on c7 and the knight on e5. In the game Black pushed the f-pawn. Find the move the engine prefers.

claims.statement: At depth 16 the rook move to e8 from a8 is the engine's best.
At depth 16 the pawn push to f4 is at least 1.5 pawns worse than the best move.
After 23...f4 24.Bxf4 Rxf4 the rook on f4 is attacked by the queen and defended by nothing.

hints: The pawn push attacks the queen, but what does it open for White's bishop?
After the push, the bishop on c1 sees the pawn on f4.
Rook a8 to e8.
items.explain: The push f4 attacks the queen, but the bishop on c1 takes the pawn, and if the rook takes the bishop, the queen takes the rook, which nothing defends: White gives a bishop for a pawn and a rook. The calm rook move to e8 keeps every piece defended and uses the open file. At depth 16 the push is at least 1.5 pawns worse.

feedback_by_move.f5f4: The pawn attacks the queen, but Bxf4 wins the pawn, and after Rxf4 the queen takes the rook: Black loses material.
feedback_by_move.e5f3: A check, but after gxf3 White keeps the bigger centre and the engine rates it more than a pawn below Re8.

items.prompt: White to move, move 10. The queens are off and Black's king is on e8. Masters most often play the quiet h3. Find one of four sound moves.

claims.statement: At depth 16 h3, Rd1, a4 and Ne2 are all within 0.12 pawns of the engine's best.

hints: Nothing is attacked and nothing is threatened. Which moves improve a piece or prepare a pawn push?
Rd1 uses the open file, h3 prevents a knight jump, a4 starts a pawn push, Ne2 reroutes the knight.
h3, Rd1, a4 or Ne2.
items.explain: Black's king is safe in the ending but has no castling right, and the d-file is open. White can take it with the rook, stop a knight from g4, advance on the queenside or reroute the knight. At depth 16 all four are within 0.12 pawns of each other.

items.prompt: White to move, move 21. The a-file is open and the rook on a4 is attacked. Find the move the engine prefers.

claims.statement: At depth 16 the rook move to a7 is the engine's best (the next best, Ra1, is 0.13 pawns lower).
After the move the rook on a7 attacks the pawn on c7.
No black piece defends the pawn on c7.

hints: Which file is open for the rook? Where does it stop on the seventh rank?
From a7 the rook attacks c7, and the bishop on d7 does not defend it.
Rook a4 to a7.
items.explain: The a-file is open, so the rook can go to a7. From there it attacks the pawn on c7, which no black piece defends, so Black has to answer at once. At depth 16 the rook move to a7 is the engine's first choice, ahead of the retreat Ra1.

items.prompt: Black to move, move 25. The rook on a7 attacks a pawn. In the game the king stepped forward. Find the move the engine prefers.

claims.statement: At depth 16 the bishop retreat to d8 is the engine's best.
The rook on a7 attacks the pawn on c7.
After the bishop retreat it defends the pawn on c7.
At depth 16 the king move to d7 is at least 0.5 pawns worse than the best move.

hints: Which pawn is attacked, and which pieces could defend it?
A bishop can defend c7 from d8 without the king having to step forward.
Bishop h4 to d8.
items.explain: The bishop on h4 retreats to d8 and defends c7, so the king can stay on e8. The king move to d7 also defends c7, but it steps onto the square where the pawn push to e6 comes with check and attacks f7 as well. At depth 16 the king move is at least half a pawn worse.

feedback_by_move.e8d7: The king defends c7 but steps onto d7, where the pawn push to e6 comes with check and also attacks the pawn on f7.

items.prompt: White to move, move 26. Black's king has stepped to d7. Find the move the engine prefers.

claims.statement: At depth 16 the pawn move to e6 is the engine's best.
After the push the pawn on e6 attacks the king on d7.
After the push the pawn on e6 also attacks the pawn on f7.

hints: The pawn on e5 has a square in front of it. What does it attack from there?
From e6 the pawn attacks d7 and f7.
Pawn e5 to e6.
items.explain: The pawn on e6 attacks the king on d7 and the pawn on f7 at the same time. Black has to deal with the check, so the pawn on f7 falls. At depth 16 the push is the engine's first choice, well ahead of the next best move.

items.prompt: White to move, move 10. White owns the bishop pair after the trade on f3. Three moves lie within a quarter of a pawn of each other; the game move is h4. Find any of the three.

claims.statement: At depth 16 d3, Bxc6 and h4 are within 0.25 pawns of the engine's best.

hints: Each move prepares something: a pawn break, a trade of the bishop, or a pawn storm.
d3 supports e4, Bxc6 changes the structure, h4 starts an attack.
d3, Bxc6 or h4.
items.explain: The pawn on d3 supports e4 and frees the bishop on c1. The capture on c6 would double Black's pawns. The pawn on h4 takes control of g5 and begins a kingside advance. At depth 16 each is within a quarter of a pawn of the best, so the choice is about plans, not safety.

items.prompt: Black to move, move 24. White's rook has come to e4 and aims at e6. In the game Black pushed the f-pawn. Find one of four moves the engine rates about equally (within 0.4 pawns).

claims.statement: At depth 16 Ne5, Re8, Nc5 and Bf8 are all within 0.4 pawns of the best move.
At depth 16 the pawn push to f5 is at least a pawn worse than the best move.

hints: The rook on e4 wants to reach e6. Which Black move covers e6 or hits the rook?
The knight can jump to e5 or c5, the rook can contest the e-file, or the bishop can retreat to f8.
Ne5, Nc5, Re8 or Bf8.
items.explain: The rook on e4 aims for e6. The push f5 attacks it, but the rook simply jumps to e6, where it attacks the pawn on d6. The four better moves, the knight to e5 or c5, the rook to e8 or the bishop back to f8, keep the e-file covered. At depth 16 the push is at least a pawn worse.

feedback_by_move.f7f5: The pawn attacks the rook, but the rook jumps to e6 and attacks d6, and the pawn on f5 and the square e6 become targets.
